pass_a_gloss: And he-set darkness hiding-place of-him, around of-him the tent of-him. He-set the darkness hiding-place of-him, middle of-himself both and of-us having-placed, as Moses of-old the veil middle of-himself both and of-hardening of-Israel, if-not easily might-see dark nature, the stored-up beauty not easily having-attained, easily also it-casts-off, through the ease of-the creation. Through this middle of-us both and of-God the bodily this stands gloom, as the cloud the of-old of-the Egyptians and of-the Hebrews; and this is perhaps which he-set darkness hiding-place of-him. Wherefore also Paul says: The only having immortality, and light dwelling unapproachable.
pass_b_english: “And he set darkness his hiding-place, around him his tent” (Psalm 17:12).

He set the darkness his hiding-place, having placed it in the middle of himself and us, as Moses of old the veil in the middle of himself and the hardening of Israel, unless a dark nature easily sees — not easily attaining the stored-up beauty, it also easily casts it off, because of the ease of the creation. Therefore in the middle of us and God this bodily gloom stands, as the cloud of old of the Egyptians and the Hebrews; and this is perhaps “he set darkness his hiding-place.” Therefore also Paul says: “Who alone has immortality, and dwells in unapproachable light” (1 Timothy 6:16).
